verdict: Caution: lend selectively to formulation units and API makers with clean USFDA/state records and verified input-tax records; avoid any borrower linked to the NCB property freeze or with unexplained asset build-up.
title: Mohali Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A Mohali pharma unit buys APIs, excipients and solvents, runs them through reaction, drying, milling and packing, and sells either bulk API to formulators or finished doses to distributors and institutions. **Cash is made in the conversion spread, not in the molecule** — so the credit question is always whether the borrower controls its input cost and its customer, or is squeezed between both. API imports are dominated by China at 65-70% of India's total [11], so a Mohali API maker's margin moves with import landed cost and FX, not with its own pricing. Collect from customer: product mix, import share of raw material, and customer-wise concentration. ## Where value and cash actually sit
Working capital is the business. Peer rating work shows working capital intensity of 48% in 7MFY2021, down from 77% in FY2018, and still described as high [10]; a contract-research peer ran revenues of Rs. 61.0 crore in FY2024 with high customer concentration [8]. **So when a proposal lands, check receivable days and inventory holding against these benchmarks; if receivable days exceed the peer range, ask for the ageing and the top-five buyer list before sanctioning.** Capex is lumpy and back-ended — one peer carries term loans of Rs. 152 crore with repayments starting May 2025 [9] — so match tenor to the plant, never fund a reactor out of a working-capital line. ## What has changed now
Two things. First, enforcement: the NCB froze 25 properties worth Rs 20.10 crore, most in Mohali, in a pharmaceutical drug diversion case, with industrial plots and commercial units at Gillco Industrial Park, Janta Industrial Estate and JLPL among them [1]. **Any borrower, promoter or family member appearing in that property list is an automatic decline, whatever the financials say.** Second, demand is real but the national picture is stretched: bank credit is up 21.6% YoY against output down 2.1% [D]. Punjab GST is running +9.7% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind, while Punjab electricity demand grew 8.8% versus India's 9.5% [D] — neutral. ## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
Peers are expanding: Aarti Pharmalabs posted record quarterly revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [4][6], and RPG Life Sciences targets 25% API growth with an acquisition within 12 months [5]. **Pursue Mohali API and CDMO units supplying such expanding buyers, and formulation makers with domestic institutional orders; avoid traders with no plant, and any unit whose only collateral is property in the frozen localities [1].** Structure as cash-flow lending against verified GST turnover, with a receivables-backed drawing power. Take monthly GSTR-2B versus purchase register, stock statement, and a quarterly plant visit with effluent and drug-licence checks. ## Early warning signs
- GST return vs bank credit turnover divergence (monthly): gap beyond 10% -> freeze limit and seek explanation. - Receivable days drift (monthly): rising two quarters running -> shift to LC-backed sales. - Customer concentration (quarterly): top buyer above 40% of sales -> cap exposure. - Any promoter name in an NDPS or NCB order (event-based): immediate stop and legal review [1].

two-quarter rise -> reduce drawing power, move to LC sales
above 40% -> cap exposure and seek diversification plan
